title: Getting started with the tumr package
text: One primary analysis tools tumr rfeat() function, implements response feature analysis. two-stage approach simplifies complex longitudinal data extracting single interpretable summary measure per subject. Specifically, rfeat(): Computes growth slope (beta coefficient) subject Averages slopes within treatment group Compares group-level summaries using one following methods: t-test ANOVA Tukey post-hoc test ANOVA Tukey post-hoc tests example uses comparison = “” perform ANOVA followed Tukey post-hoc comparisons. plot() method rfeat objects displays individual subject slopes group-level means.

title: Getting started with the tumr package
text: tumr package also includes lmm(), fits linear mixed effects model tumor growth data. Linear mixed models well suited longitudinal data account : Fixed effects: population-level effects interest (e.g., treatment, time) Random effects: subject-specific variability induces correlation among repeated measurements default, lmm() fits model: log(measure) ~ group * time + (time | id) specification allows subject growth trajectory estimating overall treatment effects. model formula can customized desired. code: library(tumr) data("melanoma2")  # Create a tumr object (Both quoted and unquoted names are supported.) melanoma2$months <- melanoma2$Day / (365/12) mel2 <- tumr(melanoma2, ID, months, Volume, Treatment) mel2 <- tumr(melanoma2, "ID", "months", "Volume", "Treatment")  # Visualization (Original scale and Log scale) plot(mel2, par = TRUE) plot(mel2, par = TRUE, fold = TRUE) plot(mel2, par = TRUE) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10() plot(mel2, par = TRUE, fold = TRUE) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10()  # Response feature analysis rfeat_mel2 <- rfeat(mel2, comparison = "both") plot(rfeat_mel2)  # Linear mixed-effects modeling lmm_obj <- lmm(mel2) summary(lmm_obj) plot(lmm_obj, "response") plot(lmm_obj, "slope")  # Nonlinear model - Exponential quadratic model quad_obj <- quad(mel2) plot(quad_obj, "predict") plot(quad_obj, "contrast")  # Nonlinear model - Generalized Addictive Model gam_obj <- tumr_gam(mel2) plot(gam_obj, "predict") plot(gam_obj, "contrast")  # Compute Tumor Doubling Time based on Linear mixed-effects modeling dtime(lmm_obj)
